body: Damage to infrastructure and the contamination of
main
food supplies are
just two of the many
negative effects of global warming
and the melting of sea ice
on remote northern communities.
Alaska Natives’ subsistence culture is being threatened by the decline in Arctic sea ice
, which has made it more challenging to travel and hunt throughout the winter months and gather the necessary resources and food required for survival (Brown et al., 2018). Between 2002 and 2017,
the Yup’ik indigenous people of Newtok
, a coastal settlement in western Alaska,
were confronted with substantial difficulties stemming from climate-related change.

During this time, six significant storms exacerbated erosion and permafrost degradation by flooding the village’s water supply and spreading untreated sewage throughout the community. Because of these natural disasters,
residents
were compelled to evacuate their homes, which led to losing their food supplies and suspending services necessary for survival
Having a safe place
individuals can call home
and feel comfortable
is essential to
their
health and well-being
. Newtok has been striving to get its constituents out of the path of climate change for
over a handful of y
ears, but neither the state nor the federal government can help communities in flood-prone regions relocate, restore, or improve infrastructure in the aftermath of natural disasters

(Bronen, 2021; Chapin et al., 2022). Other Alaskan communities, such as Shishmaref, Quinhagak, and Kivalina, have encountered the same difficulty in relocating their inhabitants and have been unsuccessful.
As a result of climate change,
31 indigenous communities could be
forcibly displaced
, and 184 of the state’s 213 rural communities could be obliterated due to flooding and erosion, resulting in increased homelessness and cultural loss
(Norton Smith et al., 2016). Alaska Natives have thrived for millennia due to centuries of keen observation and intimate engagement with their natural surroundings; however,
climate-related circumstances have led to significant population loss due to factors such as famine or starvation, the spread of disease, relocation, and homelessness
(Brown et al., 2018; Hensley et al., 2018; Hueffer et al., 2019).
